tokens.TITLE: Shane Boyer x YSL: Saint Laurent FW23
tokens.META_DESCRIPTION: Shane Boyer (@shaneboyerr) shot Saint Laurent FW23 through his cinematic POV lens. Inside the YSL fashion film and why luxury booked a New York POV creator.
tokens.KEYWORDS: Shane Boyer, shaneboyerr, Shane Boyer YSL, Saint Laurent, YSL FW23, fashion film, POV filmmaker, TikTok, New York creator, luxury influencer marketing
tokens.DEK: Luxury usually wants gloss. Shane Boyer gave YSL something rarer for FW23 — a cinematic, first-person film that looks like his New York, with Saint Laurent inside it. Proof that a POV creator can carry a fashion house.
tokens.HERO_CAPTION: Shane Boyer's Saint Laurent FW23 fashion film. Courtesy @shaneboyerr — see more on his TikTok.
tokens.STAT_FOOTNOTE: Follower/like figures verified July 2026 (TikTok @shaneboyerr, Instagram @shaneboyer_). The Saint Laurent FW23 film is part of Boyer's fashion portfolio, supplied via DGTL.
tokens.LEAD: Fashion houses can buy gloss anywhere. What they can't buy easily is a point of view — which is why Saint Laurent's FW23 moment sits so well in the hands of Shane Boyer (@shaneboyerr). His YSL fashion film doesn't imitate a runway edit; it looks like Boyer's cinematic New York, with the brand folded into a world that already commands 2.5M+ followers.
tokens.BODY_1: That's a different value proposition than a red-carpet placement. Boyer's audience shows up for mood and craft — patient, colour-graded, first-person footage. Put YSL inside that language and the luxury reads as taste rather than a logo drop. For a house courting a younger, film-literate audience, that translation is the whole point.
tokens.BODY_2: Boyer's signature is restraint — he holds a frame until it feels like a memory. Applied to fashion, that patience flatters the clothes without shouting about them. The Saint Laurent film reads as an art piece a viewer chooses to watch, not an ad they scroll past, and it lives in the same feed as his most-shared New York work, so it inherits that audience's attention.
tokens.PULLQUOTE: He didn't copy a runway edit. He made YSL look like his New York.
tokens.PULLQUOTE_CITE: — The DGTL Influence view on Shane Boyer x YSL
tokens.H2_2: Why a fashion house books a POV creator
tokens.BODY_3: Because reach alone is cheap and taste is not. A house like Saint Laurent gains more from one creator whose aesthetic already signals discernment than from a wall of generic placements. Boyer brings a film-maker's eye and an audience that trusts it — the exact combination that makes luxury feel discovered instead of sold. You can see the range on his TikTok and Instagram.
tokens.CALLOUT_1: A point of view money can't easily buy — cinematic, first-person restraint.
tokens.CALLOUT_2: Luxury translated into content his audience already chooses to watch.
tokens.CALLOUT_3: A film-literate 2.5M+ audience courting exactly the demo fashion wants.
tokens.CALLOUT_4: The brand reads as taste, not a logo drop.
tokens.BODY_4: It's the case for creator-led luxury in one film: hand the brief to someone whose eye already signals quality, and let the clothes live inside their world. Saint Laurent got a POV, not a placement.
tokens.STATCALLOUT_CAP: 2.5M+ who came for the craft. Boyer's audience shows up for mood and taste — the exact context a fashion house wants a product seen in.

tokens.FAQ_Q1: What did Shane Boyer do for YSL?
tokens.FAQ_A1: Shane Boyer (@shaneboyerr) created a cinematic fashion film tied to Saint Laurent's FW23, shot in his signature first-person POV style rather than as a conventional runway edit. It sits within his broader fashion and New York portfolio.
tokens.FAQ_Q2: Why would a luxury brand like Saint Laurent work with Shane Boyer?
tokens.FAQ_A2: Because Boyer brings a filmmaker's point of view and a film-literate audience of 2.5M+. His restrained, cinematic style makes luxury read as taste rather than a logo drop, reaching a younger, discerning demo that fashion houses court.
tokens.FAQ_Q3: Where can I see Shane Boyer's fashion work?

tokens.FAQ_A4: Shane Boyer is an American content creator and POV filmmaker known for cinematic New York City videos, with 2.5M+ TikTok followers. His brand work has spanned Saint Laurent (YSL), Polaroid, Canada Goose and Ray-Ban Meta.
